reasons.text: Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 245% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
85% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Category III share of certificates is 44%, +42% versus what its process route can produce
Uploaded plant photos are near-duplicates of photos registered by 1 other plant(s)
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.37x the cost floor)
Sold products equal only 37% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed

inspection_checklist: Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Compare the plant against the entities sharing its identifiers (bank, address, director, photos); consider a joint inspection.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
